findings.finding: StateChat, the State Department's internally built ChatGPT-like enterprise chatbot launched in August 2024, is available to the entire State Department workforce of more than 75,000 employees worldwide.
findings.estimated_users: available to 75,000+ employees worldwide (entire workforce); reported adoption of 45,000-50,000 cumulative users by Sept 2025
findings.exact_quote: StateChat, a ChatGPT-like interface launched in August that leverages Palantir and Azure OpenAI, a spokesperson confirmed, and is currently available to the more than 75,000 State Department employees around the world.
findings.source_title: From translation to email drafting, State Department turns to AI to assist workforce, FedScoop
findings.notes: COVERAGE CHANGED most->all (prior pass). The 'most' tag conflated availability with adoption. FedScoop (Dec 11, 2024, Madison Alder) states verbatim that StateChat 'is currently available to the more than 75,000 State Department employees around the world' -- availability is the entire workforce, so 'all'. FedScoop + Nextgov re-checked 2026-05-21: confirmed still department-wide and growing. FedScoop (Apr 14, 2026, Matt Bracken, 'State Department eyes agentic AI for taking on high-volume workflows') reports StateChat 'has roughly 58,000 users and is being used in ... over 98% of our 270 missions and posts around the globe' and saves 20,000-30,000 hours/week -- newer adoption metrics, not a coverage change. Note: per Nextgov (Mar 10, 2026, DiMolfetta/Kelley) and FedScoop, State switched StateChat's underlying model from Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5 to OpenAI GPT-4.1 in Mar 2026 per a presidential directive; the tool itself remains available department-wide. coverage stays 'all'.

findings.finding: StateChat adoption has grown from 45,000-50,000 users (Sept 2025) to roughly 58,000 users by April 2026, with usage in over 98% of the department's 270 missions and posts worldwide; the department estimates it saves 20,000-30,000 hours per week.
findings.estimated_users: ~58,000 users (Apr 2026; up from 45,000-50,000 in Sept 2025); used in 98%+ of 270 missions/posts
findings.exact_quote: which Ritualo said has roughly 58,000 users and is "being used in … over 98% of our 270 missions and posts around the globe."
findings.source_title: State Department eyes agentic AI for taking on 'high-volume workflows', FedScoop
findings.notes: This row records ADOPTION metrics, kept separate so availability-vs-adoption stays explicit. Updated 2026-05-21 with the newest FedScoop source (Apr 14, 2026, Matt Bracken): adoption rose to ~58,000 users (vs 45,000-50,000 in the Sept 2025 Nextgov story), used in 98%+ of 270 missions/posts, saving 20,000-30,000 hours/week. coverage_assessment stays 'all' -- availability remains the entire ~75,000-80,000 workforce. Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21.

findings.tool_name: Department-wide generative AI platform (no confirmed agency-wide tool)
findings.finding: The Department of the Interior's September 2025 AI Strategy describes DOI as still building the foundation for enterprise-wide AI use, moving from bureau-specific pilots toward a mature coordinated capability; there is no publicly confirmed agency-wide general-purpose AI platform available to all employees.
findings.exact_quote: The Department is building the foundation for enterprise-wide use of Artificial Intelligence. The goal is to move from bureau-specific pilots to a mature, coordinated capability that supports the full lifecycle of AI development and deployment.
findings.source_title: Department of the Interior Artificial Intelligence Strategy: Setting the Vision
findings.notes: COVERAGE CHANGED most->partial (prior pass). The 'most' tag rested on an uncorroborated OMB-inventory '50,000+' self-report. DOI's AI Strategy (Sept 30, 2025) describes a pilots-to-enterprise transition, not a completed rollout. Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21: FedScoop's most recent DOI AI coverage (Feb 18, 2026, Lindsey Wilkinson, 'Interior Department finding momentum with modernization') reports DOI 'exploring emerging technologies, such as generative AI' and 200+ inventory use cases plus RPA bots (Bob, Bobby, Oz) for procurement -- it does NOT report any department-wide general-purpose AI chatbot available to all employees, consistent with the 'partial' tag. No Nextgov DOI-specific deployment story found. coverage stays 'partial'.

findings.tool_name: Microsoft Copilot / Copilot Chat, Synthesia (OMB inventory entry)
findings.finding: DOI's 2025 OMB AI use case inventory self-reports Microsoft Copilot/Copilot Chat plus Synthesia at the 50,000+ user band for written communications, but no press release or official document independently corroborates that figure.
findings.notes: COVERAGE CHANGED most->partial (prior pass). Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21: no DOI-specific Copilot enterprise-rollout announcement found in either outlet. FedScoop's Feb 18, 2026 DOI modernization story does not report a DOI Copilot deployment. The '50,000+' rests solely on the self-reported inventory entry, best read as a license-availability count under the government-wide M365 Copilot OneGov offer, not a verified enterprise deployment to all employees. DOI's AI Strategy frames current use as bureau-specific pilots not yet standardized. Quote/url null per searched_no_source rule.

findings.finding: DHSChat, DHS's internally built secure generative AI chatbot, was rolled out department-wide beyond its initial ~19,000-employee headquarters launch and is available to DHS staff across the department.
findings.estimated_users: department-wide availability (DHS workforce ~260,000); the initial 2024 headquarters launch covered ~19,000 employees
findings.notes: COVERAGE CHANGED partial->all. The department-wide rollout of DHSChat beyond its initial ~19,000-employee DHS headquarters launch is attested by the DHS AI Corps program lead (the program owner) as a primary source. Public reporting has not yet caught up: the most recent public scope statement (FedScoop, May 22, 2025, 'Homeland Security cuts off access to ChatGPT and other commercial AI') still describes DHSChat as available to 'the nearly 20,000 employees at DHS headquarters', and the original launch was reported by Nextgov (Dec 17, 2024, https://www.nextgov.com/artificial-intelligence/2024/12/dhs-launches-internal-genai-chatbot-leverage-non-public-data/401733/) as '~19,000 employees at DHS headquarters and select pilot users across ten operating agencies'. Recorded as coverage 'all' with source_type 'primary_attestation' and confidence 'medium' to flag that this rests on a first-hand account rather than a published source; a public-source update is pending.

findings.tool_name: Commercial generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot Chat) - pre-DHSChat program
findings.finding: Before DHSChat, DHS spent a year allowing employees to use commercial generative AI tools on publicly available information only, training thousands of staff; DHS later cut off access to commercial tools like ChatGPT.
findings.exact_quote: Last year, we began allowing employees to use commercial generative AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude on publicly available information only; thousands of employees have now received training and use these tools to support their work.
findings.source_title: DHS's Responsible Use of Generative AI Tools, CSIAC (DTIC)
findings.notes: COVERAGE UNCHANGED: partial. Commercial-AI access at DHS was opt-in/training-gated and reached 'thousands' of trained employees, a defined subset, hence 'partial'. Quote verified verbatim against the CSIAC/DTIC (.mil) republication carried over from prior agent2 verification (original HSToday URL 403s). Note FedScoop separately reported DHS later cut off employee access to commercial tools like ChatGPT, so the commercial picture at DHS has shifted; DHSChat is now the primary internal tool.

findings.tool_name: Microsoft Copilot / OpenAI models / Grok (optional generative AI tools)
findings.finding: USDA offers Microsoft Copilot, OpenAI models and (newly) xAI's Grok as optional generative AI tools for trained internal employees; no public source confirms how many of USDA's ~100,000 employees can access them or states agency-wide availability.
findings.estimated_users: subset of ~100,000 workforce; gated to trained internal employees, exact count not disclosed
findings.exact_quote: Grok will be available as an optional tool on the same basis as Copilot and OpenAI models for data analysis, scientific research, conservation planning, agricultural modeling, operational efficiency, and anything that trained internal USDA employees see fit.
findings.source_title: Agriculture Department plans to use Grok, despite growing concerns over the chatbot, Fast Company
findings.notes: COVERAGE UNCHANGED: partial (re-verified). Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21. FedScoop's most recent USDA AI story (Apr 13, 2026, Lindsey Wilkinson, 'Grok-maker xAI gets USDA backing in pursuit of FedRAMP High authorization') confirms USDA is sponsoring Grok's FedRAMP High pursuit but gives no employee access-scope detail. Nextgov's May 19, 2026 OIG story (Natalie Alms) reports USDA 'doesn't even have a generative AI policy at all' and is 'at risk of shadow AI' relying on an annual self-report data call -- reinforcing an ungoverned/non-standardized posture, NOT an agency-wide rollout. The access-scope quote (gating Copilot/OpenAI/Grok to 'trained internal USDA employees', all 'optional') remains the Fast Company exclusive (May 2025); no FedScoop/Nextgov source supersedes it. The OMB inventory '50,000+' Copilot Chat band is an uncorroborated self-report and cannot support 'most'. coverage stays 'partial'; confidence low.

findings.finding: DOJ has not announced a deliberate department-wide general-purpose AI rollout, but as a Microsoft 365 agency its staff have latent access to Copilot Chat (with commercial data protection) through existing M365 licensing; no public source documents an intentional agency-wide deployment or a user-count band.
findings.notes: COVERAGE CHANGED unknown->latent. DOJ's 2025 OMB inventory lists Microsoft Copilot use but no user-count band, and the FedScoop + Nextgov re-check (2026-05-21) found only specialized DOJ AI tools (case-information generative AI deployed June 2025, PATTERN recidivism tool, facial recognition, litigation support) and no general-purpose employee chat-assistant rollout. FedScoop's most recent DOJ AI-inventory coverage (Feb 11, 2026, Miranda Nazzaro) reports 315 use cases but no agency-wide chat assistant. However, DOJ is a Microsoft 365 agency, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (with commercial data protection) is available to any M365-licensed user -- so DOJ staff have *latent* access even absent a deliberate departmental rollout. Tagged 'latent' rather than 'unknown' to record this specific characterized state: an M365 Copilot Chat entitlement exists, but no intentional agency-wide deployment is documented. Status stays 'searched_no_source' -- no public source attests a deliberate rollout.

findings.finding: DOT's Volpe Center built and launched chat.dot.gov, the department's first employee-facing AI chatbot, as a technology demonstrator that reached a user base of more than 5,000 users, with the beta later expanded to all operating administrations.
findings.exact_quote: the U.S. DOT Volpe Center developed chat.dot.gov, a web-based chatbot for U.S. DOT employees
findings.source_title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence at U.S. Department of Transportation, Volpe National Transportation Systems Center
findings.notes: COVERAGE UNCHANGED: partial (re-verified for the chat.dot.gov demonstrator specifically). Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21. The volpe.dot.gov page bot-blocks direct WebFetch (403); WebSearch of the page corroborates chat.dot.gov is 'the U.S. DOT's first AI-powered chatbot for its employees', 'a successful AI technology demonstrator' that 'reached a user base of more than 5,000 users' averaging '900 simultaneous active users daily', with the beta 'expansion ... to all operating administrations'. exact_quote kept as the short verbatim phrase. 5,000+ users against a ~55,000 DOT workforce, explicitly a 'technology demonstrator' -- 'partial' is correct FOR THIS TOOL. IMPORTANT: the Volpe page itself notes 'While the specific chat.dot.gov platform has evolved as the Department expands its AI capacity to support additional tools' -- DOT's general-purpose generative-AI availability has since moved to department-wide Google Gemini (see the separate DOT Gemini finding, tagged 'most'). This row is retained as the historical demonstrator; the live agency-wide picture is captured by the Gemini finding.

findings.tool_name: Google Gemini (department-wide via Google Workspace migration)
findings.finding: DOT migrated from Microsoft to Google Workspace under a five-year, up-to-$89M contract and provided agency-wide access to Google Gemini and NotebookLM within 60 days; the rollout reached ~12,500 DOT-proper employees at a February 2026 'global go-live', with the FAA and remaining staff (totaling more than 50,000 employees) to follow shortly after.
findings.estimated_users: agency-wide access provided; ~12,500 DOT-proper employees live Feb 2026, FAA + remainder following (~50,000+ total workforce)
findings.exact_quote: Transportation migrated initial users to Workspace within 30 days and provided agency-wide access to Gemini and NotebookLM within 60 days.
findings.source_title: Inside the Transportation Department's technology transformation, Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: COVERAGE CHANGED unknown->most. Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21 and found a material development: DOT became the first cabinet-level agency to move its whole workforce to Google Workspace with Gemini (GSA OneGov, five-year contract up to $89M signed Sept 2025). Nextgov (Dec 29, 2025, Frank Konkel) states verbatim DOT 'provided agency-wide access to Gemini and NotebookLM within 60 days', with a 'global go-live for 12,500 DOT-proper employees in February 2026 and a subsequent rollout shortly after for the Federal Aviation Administration and remaining staff, totaling more than 50,000 employees.' FedScoop (Dec 5, 2025, Lindsey Wilkinson) corroborates: ~12,000 employees onboarded with 40,000 more planned within a year. Tagged 'most' rather than 'all' because, as of the most recent (Dec 2025/Feb 2026) reporting, DOT-proper was live but FAA + remaining staff were still rolling out -- an in-progress agency-wide deployment trending toward 'all'. This supersedes the prior 'unknown' tag, which predated the Workspace/Gemini migration and only knew of chat.dot.gov. NOTE: most recent confirming source is Dec 29, 2025 (~5 months old) -- FAA-stage completion not yet press-confirmed; revisit for a post-Feb-2026 source.

findings.finding: The IRS purchased 150 ChatGPT Enterprise licenses for use within the Treasury Department through a federal contractor, and Treasury tested ChatGPT among a small user base; federal spending records show a Treasury official later approved acquiring up to 3,000 licenses.
findings.estimated_users: 150 licenses verified initially; reporting of up to 3,000 licenses approved subsequently (Treasury workforce ~100,000, mostly IRS)
findings.exact_quote: the Internal Revenue Service purchased 150 ChatGPT Enterprise Licenses for use within the Department of the Treasury through a federal contractor, though it's not clear how many were or have been used.
findings.source_title: OpenAI further expands its generative AI work with the federal government, FedScoop
findings.notes: COVERAGE UNCHANGED: pilot (re-verified). Checked FedScoop + Nextgov 2026-05-21. FedScoop (Nov 5, 2024, original quote) carries the 150-license quote verbatim. The most recent FedScoop Treasury coverage (Jan 29, 2026, Matt Bracken, 'IRS ramps up AI use amid staff cuts, Treasury inventory shows') reports Treasury more than doubled AI use cases (54 -> 129) and lists specialized IRS tools (NLP for employee questions, IaaP Accelerator agentic tool, IT-service-desk gen AI) but does NOT report a general-purpose enterprise chat assistant available department-wide. FedScoop (June 9, 2025, Billy Mitchell) shows Treasury was still SEEKING general-purpose chat assistants and had only limited FAQ pilots ('Winnie'). Verified named-commercial-tool procurement remains 150 ChatGPT Enterprise licenses, Treasury 'test[ing] ChatGPT among a small user base'. Separate Fast Company reporting on up to 3,000 ChatGPT licenses is still ~3% of the ~100,000 (mostly IRS) workforce. Best public characterization: pilot. Note: Treasury is shedding Anthropic/Claude contracts per the 2026 presidential directive (Nextgov, Mar 2026), and the GSA-OpenAI OneGov $1/agency offer remains an opt-in availability offer, not a Treasury-confirmed enterprise rollout. coverage stays 'pilot'.
